careerInfoDesignation: Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Mr. Hagiuda has served as member of Japan’s House of Representatives since 2003. He is currently serving his 6th term in the House of Representatives, representing Tokyo’s 24th district. Previously, he served as an elected official on the Metropolitan Assembly of Tokyo and Hachioji City Council.Immediately prior to his current appointments, Mr. Hagiuda served as Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) and Minister in charge of Education Rebuilding, positions he held since September 2019. Previously, Mr. Hagiuda held several senior posts in the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP). Earlier in his career, Mr. Hagiuda served as Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology.Mr. Hagiuda Koichi was appointed Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) on October 4, 2021. He also assumed the roles of Minister in charge of Industrial Competitiveness, Minister for Economic Cooperation with Russia, Minister in charge of the Response to the Economic Impact caused by the Nuclear Accident, Minister for Green Transformation and Minister of State for the Nuclear Damage Compensation and Decommissioning Facilitation Corporation.
educationInfo: A graduate of Meiji University’s School of Commerce
summary: Hagiuda Koichi is the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Before seeking public office, Mr. Hosoda was a civil servant, joining MITI (now METI) right after graduating from Kyoto University’s Faculty of Law. Mr. Hosoda is also a graduate of Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government where he earned a Master in Public Administration.Prior to his current appointment, Mr. Hosoda served in several senior posts within the Liberal Democratic Party including Deputy Chief Secretary, Research Commission on Comprehensive Energy Strategy and Director and Acting Director, Agriculture and Forestry Division. Mr. Hosoda has also served on key committees at the House of Representatives, including the Special Committee for the Investigation of Nuclear Power Issues.Mr. Hosoda Kenichi was appointed State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry on 6, October, 2021. He joins the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) from the House of Representatives where he is currently serving his fourth term of office.
educationInfo: Before seeking public office, Mr. Hosoda was a civil servant, joining MITI (now METI) right after graduating from Kyoto University’s Faculty of Law. Mr. Hosoda is also a graduate of Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government where he earned a Master in Public Administration.
summary: Hosoda Kenichi is the State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Before seeking elected office, Mr. Ishii served as a civil servant at the Ministry of Construction (now the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism).A member of Japan’s House of Councillors representing Okayama Prefecture, Mr. Ishii joins the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry after serving in several key posts in the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP). Mr. Ishii is currently serving in his second term in the House of Councillors. Prior to representing Okayama Prefecture in the House of Councillors, Mr.Ishii served as Governor of Okayama Prefecture for four consecutive terms.  Mr. Ishii was appointed to the three senior roles of State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI); State Minister of the Cabinet Office; and Director-General, Local Nuclear Emergency Response Headquarters on October 6, 2021.
educationInfo: A graduate of Tokyo University’s Faculty of Law
summary: Ishii Masahiro is the State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Prior to seeking national elected office, Mr. Iwata worked as a management consultant at the Ohmae & Associates Group.Earlier in his career as a publicly elected official, Mr. Iwata served as a member of the Saga Prefectural assembly.Immediately prior to his appointment to the Ministry of Economy Trade and Industry (METI), Mr. Iwata served on senior posts in the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) including Chairperson, of Committee on Organizations Involved with Commerce, Industry and Medium and Small Sized Enterprises as well as Deputy Director, Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism Division. In 2019, he was appointed Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Defense.Mr. Iwata was appointed Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry on October 6, 2021. A member of Japan’s House of Representatives, Mr. Iwata represents the Saga 1st district as part of the Kyushu proportional bloc. He is currently serving his fourth term in office.
educationInfo: A graduate of Kyushu University’s Faculty of Law
summary: Iwata Kazuchika is the Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Before seeking elected office, Ms. Yoshikawa worked in the private sector including as a banker for Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.Immediately prior to her current posting at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Ms. Yoshikawa served as Deputy Director, of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) Women's Affairs Division; one of several key posts she has held in the LDP.Ms. Yoshikawa Yumi was appointed Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry on October 6,2021. She is a member of Japan’s House of Councillors, representing Mie Prefecture since 2013. Ms. Yoshikawa was the first female member of the House of Councillors from Mie Prefecture. As a member of the House of Councillors, Ms. Yoshikawa has served on several key policy committees including as Chairperson of the Committee on Education, Culture and Science and Director, Committee on Economy and Industry.
educationInfo: Yoshikawa is a graduate of the Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology’s Graduate School of Agriculture where she earned a Master’s degree
summary: Yoshikawa Yumi is the Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
careerInfo: Mr. Tada is a graduate of the University of Tokyo’s Faculty of Law. He earned a Master of International Public Policy from Johns Hopkins University’s School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS).During his time as the Deputy Commissioner of the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ANRE), Mr. Tada managed nuclear energy policy and safety. This included the restarting of nuclear energy power plants in Japan and the disposal of radioactive waste. During his tenure as ANRE’s Director-General, Electricity and Gas Industry Department, Mr. Tada reformed energy policy, including the deregulation of the electricity and gas markets.When he served as Director General, Economic and Fiscal Management Cabinet Office, Mr. Tada oversaw key economic and fiscal policies under the leadership of the Prime Minister. He also served as the Director-General of METI’s Manufacturing Industries Bureau where he led business promotion policy for Japan’s manufacturing industries.In his previous role as Deputy Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry, Mr. Tada oversaw budgets, personnel affairs, and digital transformation at METI. Mr. Tada is instrumental in planning, designing and implementing METI’s policies in these areas.Since joining METI, Mr. Tada has served in several senior posts in areas from environmental policy to SME policy. While serving as the Director of the Environmental Policy Division, he managed issues related to global warming ahead of COP 13 and the Hokkaido Toyako Summit. He also established a new financial guarantee system in response to the deterioration of cash flow to SMEs in his role as the Director of the Finance Division, SMEA.Mr. Tada Akihiro has served as a Vice-Minister of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2021. He supervises ministry affairs, including policy planning and formulation, as well as project implementation. He also leads several teams of officials supporting the Minister, State Ministers and Parliamentary Vice-Ministers.
educationInfo: Mr. Tada is a graduate of the University of Tokyo’s Faculty of Law. He earned a Master of International Public Policy from Johns Hopkins University’s School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS).
summary: Tada Akihiro is the Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry

careerInfoDesignation: Vice-Minister for International Affairs
careerInfo: From 2020, as Director-General of the Commerce and Information Policy Bureau, Mr. Hirai oversaw METI policy related to the IT industry, including cyber security and the online creative content industry.From 2019, as Deputy Commissioner for Natural Resources and Energy Policy at ANRE, Mr. Hirai was closely involved in international negotiations in the energy policy area, which contributed to the development of systems to ensure the stable supply of resources and energy.From 2018, Mr. Hirai played a key role in the government-wide economic growth strategy while serving as the Senior Councilor at Cabinet Secretariat.From 2015, as the Director-General for Nuclear Accident Disaster Response, Minister's Secretariat, Mr. Hirai managed government programs aimed at resolving the Fukushima nuclear accident, including the decontamination of the nuclear power plant and treatment of contaminated water.Since joining METI, Mr. Hirai has served in a wide range of senior posts. These include Director of the Corporate Finance and Tax Affairs Division, Business Environment Department, Small and Medium Enterprise Agency; General Manager of the Washington DC Office of Japan Oil, Gas and Metals National Corporation (JOGMEC) as well as Director of the General Affairs Division, Minister's Secretariat.Prior to his current position, Mr. Hirai was appointed Director-General of the Economic and Industrial　Policy Bureau in July 2021. As head of the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau, he coordinated METI’s economic and industrial initiatives, tax reform measures, corporate governance and support for start-up businesses.Mr. Hirai Hirohide has been serving as Vice Minister for International Affairs at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2022. He leads all of METI’s international policy operations and represents the ministry in cross-border economic dialogues and negotiations, and travels alongside the Prime Minister on overseas missions to advise on economic, trade, industrial and energy policy.
summary: Hirai Hirohide is the Vice-Minister for International Affairs

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General for Technology Policy Coordination / Industrial and Product Safety
careerInfo: Mr. Tsujimoto graduated from the Faculty of Engineering at Kyoto University where he earned his master's degree in engineering at the Graduate School of Engineering. Mr. Tsujimoto also studied at Stanford University as a visiting researcher.Between 2009 and 2011, Mr. Tsujimoto served as METI's first Director for Promoting Electric Vehicles. During that time, he helped formulate the Next-Generation Vehicles Strategy 2010 to promote the wider introduction of electric vehicles in Japan.Mr. Tsujimoto's work in the natural resources and energy areas coincided with major market changes following the Great East Japan Earthquake in 2011. It included an assignment as General Manager of JOGMEC’s Vancouver Office, the start of several roles focused on increasing imports of natural gas and minerals into Japan. Prior to this assignment, Mr. Tsujimoto developed strategies to secure Japan’s supplies of rare metals as Director of the Mineral and Natural Resources Division Previously, Mr. Tsujimoto supported efforts to promote energy efficiency measures across Japan as Director of the Energy Efficiency Division.From 2017 to 2019, Mr. Tsujimoto was in charge of human resources for METI executives. At the same time, he worked as a Counsellor for Crisis Management within METI. In this position, he managed the Ministry’s response to large-scale natural disasters including the floods in western Japan and the Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake.Since joining METI in 1992, Mr. Tsujimoto has mainly focused on the natural resources, energy and trade policy areas. Immediately prior to his current appointment, Mr. Tsujimoto was responsible for onsite measures to restore Fukushima from the damage caused by the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station accident.Mr. Tsujimoto Keisuke currently serves as the head of crisis management at METI. As well as managing the Ministry’s response to major disasters and national emergencies, he also oversees industrial and product safety and technology policy.
educationInfo: Mr. Tsujimoto graduated from the Faculty of Engineering at Kyoto University where he earned his master's degree in engineering at the Graduate School of Engineering. Mr. Tsujimoto also studied at Stanford University as a visiting researcher.
summary: Tsujimoto Keisuke is the Director-General for Technology Policy Coordination / Industrial and Product Safety

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General Fukushima Nuclear Accident Response and Reconstruction Policy
careerInfo: Mr. Sudo is a graduate of the University of Tokyo Faculty of Economics.He served as Director of the Industrial Machinery Division and Director of the Budget and Accounts Division, before assuming the office of Director of the Support Team for Nuclear Disaster Victims in 2017 and Executive Director of the Fukushima Soso Reconstruction Corporation in 2018.Since joining METI, he has served in the Industrial Structure Policy Division, as well as the Development Division of the Public Benefit Service Department, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy. He assumed the office of Deputy Director of the Industrial Safety Division in 1994. From February to March 1995, he dealt with the aftermath of the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake as a member of Minister Ozato's Special Assignment Office. He then assumed the offices of Deputy Mayor of Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture. He has also served as Director of the Industry and Labour Department and Director of the City Center Revitalization Office of Fukui Prefecture, where he helped promote local industries. Following the accident at the Tokyo Electric Power Company's Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station in 2011, he helped plan support for disaster victims and lift evacuation orders as the Director of the Support Team for Nuclear Disaster Victims of the Cabinet Office.Mr. Sudo Osamu has served as Director-General, Fukushima Nuclear Accident Response and Reconstruction Policy since July 2022. In this capacity, he is engaged in ensuring the full recovery from the aftermath of the nuclear accident in Fukushima.
educationInfo: Mr. Sudo is a graduate of the University of Tokyo Faculty of Economics.
summary: Sudo Osamu is the Director-General Fukushima Nuclear Accident Response and Reconstruction Policy

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Fukushima Reconstruction Promotion Group
careerInfo: A graduate of Kyoto University’s Faculty of Law, Mr. Kataoka holds a Master in Public Policy degree from Princeton University in the United States.Most recently, as the Director of the Personnel Division of the Minister's Secretariat, he worked on reforming METI human resources policies.In the Electricity and Gas Industry Department, he was involved in the electricity system reform and the review of the raising of electricity rates by power companies after the Great East Japan Earthquake.Since joining METI, Mr. Kataoka has held several senior posts. They have included Director of the Economic and Industrial Policy Division in the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau, Director of the Electricity Market Division in the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy's Electricity and Gas Industry Department, and Executive Secretary to the Minister of METI.Mr. Kataoka Koichiro has served as Director-General, Fukushima Reconstruction Promotion Group at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2022. He is responsible for reactor decommissioning and contaminated water management, as well as reconstruction support and industrial development in the affected areas.
educationInfo: A graduate of Kyoto University’s Faculty of Law, Mr. Kataoka holds a Master in Public Policy degree from Princeton University in the United States.
summary: Kataoka Koichiro is the Director-General, Fukushima Reconstruction Promotion Group

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau / Energy, Environmental and Innovation Policy
careerInfo: Mr. Iida is a graduate of the University of Tokyo's Faculty of Economics and Emory University’s Goizueta Business School.Earlier in his career, Mr. Iida held several key post including the Director of the Industrial Revitalization Division, the Executive Assistant to the Chief Cabinet Secretary and the Director of the Minister's Secretariat.While serving as the Director of the General Policy Division for the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy, he led the establishment of the Strategic Energy Plan, the first address the accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station, and worked to secure funding for the reconstruction of communities in Fukushima Prefecture. He also oversaw the creation of the Energy White Paper and affairs relating to COP19.Prior to this, Mr. Iida served as METI’s Personnel Division Director, promoting workstyle reform within the ministry. He also worked to strengthen human resource development through training and education, as well as optimal personnel allocation.Mr. Iida previously served as Director-General for Policy Planning and Coordination where he supervised all affairs concerning the planning and adjustment of significant policy matters under METI’s jurisdiction. He also took office as Director of the Regional Economic and Industrial Policy Group and supervised regional economic policies.Mr. Iida served as Director-General of the Industrial Science and Technology Policy and Environment Bureau at METI. As the head of this bureau, he oversaw the promotion of Japan’s national innovation strategy and the planning and implementation of national research and development projects. He also oversaw industrial standards policy and environmental policy, including Japan’s efforts to combat climate change.In his previous role as Deputy Commissioner, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy, METI, he was engaged in the planning of new energy policies toward Japan's "2050 decarbonized society."From 2021, as Deputy Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry, he oversaw budgets, personnel affairs, and digital transformation at METI. Mr. Iida was instrumental in planning, designing and implementing METI’s policies in these areas.Mr. Iida Yuji was appointed Director-General of the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau at Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) in July 2022. As head of the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau, he is responsible for coordinating METI’s economic and industrial initiatives, tax reform measures, corporate governance and support for start-up businesses.
educationInfo: Mr. Iida is a graduate of the University of Tokyo's Faculty of Economics and Emory University’s Goizueta Business School.
summary: Iida Yuji is the Director-General, Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau / Energy, Environmental and Innovation Policy

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Trade Policy Bureau
careerInfo: Mr. Matsuo graduated from the University of Tokyo with a degree in Law and from the Paul H. Nize School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) at Johns Hopkins University, with a Master in International Public Policy.From 2008 to 2010 he served as Special Advisor to the Executive Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA) in Paris and contributed to the IEA’s input to the G8 Summit in 2008.Previously, he held the position of Counsellor of the Cabinet Secretariat from 2010 to 2012 and oversaw the Japanese government’s decision to start negotiations with TPP (Trans-Pacific Partnership Agreement) member countries regarding joining the TPP.  In addition, he supervised the adjustment of electricity supply and demand in eastern Japan in the aftermath of the Great East Japan Earthquake of 2011.From 2013 to 2014, as Director of the Budget and Accounts Division, he drafted METI’s budget.He also served as Director, General Policy Division of the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy and contributed to METI’s decision-making regarding the Energy Supply and Demand Outlook for 2030, which provided fundamental mid-term policy guidance for Japan’s energy policies.He served as Secretary General of the Electricity and Gas Market Surveillance Commission (EGC) since its establishment in September 2015 and led the Secretariat to contribute to the successful and full liberalization of the electricity and gas retail markets in Japan, and to the launch of transmission and distribution charge system reform.He served as Director General for Trade Policy at the Trade Policy Bureau of METI from 2017 to 2019. He made a contribution to finalizing Japan-EU Economic Partnership Agreement as the METI’s chief negotiator and advanced the G20 Osaka process as a co-chair of the Trade and Investment Working Group.Before he was appointed to this position, he served as Director General, National Space Policy Secretariat (NSPS) of the Cabinet Office (CAO) from 2019 to 2021. He played a leading role in creating the 4th Basic Plan on the Space policy of the Japanese Government, which was decided by the cabinet in June 2020, and establish a new framework of relevant ministries to coordinate the government’s dual-use satellite technology R&D projects.Mr. Takehiko Matsuo has been working as Director General, Trade Policy Bureau, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2021.33 years of experience working for the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) as well as Cabinet Office and other agencies.
educationInfo: Mr. Matsuo graduated from the University of Tokyo with a degree in Law and from the Paul H. Nize School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) at Johns Hopkins University, with a Master in International Public Policy.
summary: Matsuo Takehiko is the Director-General, Trade Policy Bureau

summary: Kimura Satoshi is the Director-General, Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Industrial Science and Technology Policy and Environment Bureau
careerInfo: Mr. Hatakeyama graduated from The University of Tokyo’s Faculty of Law.Prior to assuming his current role, Mr. Hatakeyama oversaw policymaking across METI while serving as the Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Minister's Secretariat.In his previous role as Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Commissioner’s Secretariat, ANRE, Mr. Hatakeyama formulated the strategy for Japan’s energy policy and coordinated policy planning for budgets and taxes.During his career, Mr. Hatakeyama has held a range of key government posts. These include Director of the Policy Planning Division, Electricity and Gas Industry Department, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ANRE); Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Commissioner’s Secretariat, ANRE; as well as Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Minister's Secretariat.Mr. Hatakeyama Yojiro has served as Director-General for Commerce and Service Industry Policy since July 2020. In this role, Mr. Hatakeyama is responsible for enhancing efficiency in Japan’s distribution and services industries, expanding the use of cashless transactions in Japan and managing international trade exhibitions.
educationInfo: Mr. Hatakeyama graduated from The University of Tokyo’s Faculty of Law.
summary: Hatakeyama Yojiro is the Director-General, Industrial Science and Technology Policy and Environment Bureau

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Manufacturing Industries Bureau
careerInfo: Most recently, as the Director-General of the Industrial Science and Technology Policy and Environment Bureau, and Deputy Commissioner of the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy, he has been working on policies toward carbon neutrality and energy security.In 2011, following the TEPCO accident in Fukushima, he began working on establishing the Nuclear Damage Compensation and Decommissioning Facilitation Corporation (NDF). He then went on to serve as the Director of the Iron and Steel Division, Director of the Economic and Industrial Policy Division, Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division in the Minister's Secretariat, and Director-General of the Natural Resources and Fuel Department. Subsequently, from 2017 to 2020, he was seconded to NDF, and at the same time, served as a director and executive officer at TEPCO, working toward Fukushima's reconstruction through restructuring TEPCO's management.Between 2007 and 2010, as a Counsellor to the Permanent Delegation of Japan to the OECD, he worked on the rollout of Japan's energy policy through IEA.In 2006, he was involved in the formulation of the Asia Gateway Strategy as an Assistant to Special Advisor to the Prime Minister in the first Abe administration.Notably between 1995 and 1996, he worked toward establishing a stock option system and an angel tax system. From 2003 to 2004, he established the Industrial Revitalization Corporation, and subsequently was personally engaged in business revitalization at the organization.After entering the ministry in 1989, he has mainly been working on developing institutions for legislative progress, financial and capital markets and tax systems, etc. in order to construct corporate renewal systems including, venture creation, NPL disposal, business revitalization, and business restructuring.Mr. Yamashita Ryuichi has served as Director-General, Manufacturing Industries Bureau at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2022.
summary: Yamashita Ryuichi is the Director-General, Manufacturing Industries Bureau

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Commerce and Information Policy Bureau
careerInfo: Most recently, as the Deputy Director-General of Growth Strategy Council Bureau of the Cabinet Secretariat, Mr. Nohara implemented policy measures to support overall government growth strategies.In 2020, while serving as Deputy Director-General of the Commerce and Information Policy Bureau, Mr. Nohara worked toward the successful enactment of the Act on Promotion of Development, Supply, and Deployment of Specified Advanced Information and Communications Technology Utilization System , leaving a legacy of achievements including the establishment of a tax system to promote investment in 5G .During his time as Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division in the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau, Mr. Nohara compiled measures for future investment strategies and formulated a New Economic Policy Package linking revolutions in both productivity and human resource development to address Japan's greatest challenges; its declining birthrate and aging population. As Director of the Budget and Accounts Division of the Minister's Secretariat, he prepared budget proposals for METI.Since joining METI, Mr. Nohara has served in several senior posts including Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division in the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau and Director of the Budget and Accounts Division of the Minister's Secretariat.Mr. Nohara Satoshi was appointed Director-General of the Commerce and Information Policy Bureau at Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) in October 2021. As head of the bureau, he oversees ministry policy for digital industries including the online creative content industry as well as cyber security.
summary: Nohara Satoshi is the Director-General, Commerce and Information Policy Bureau

careerInfoDesignation: Commissioner, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy
careerInfo: Mr. Hosaka is a graduate of the University of Tokyo’s Department of Economics, Faculty of Economics, and also studied at the University of Michigan in the United States.During his career, he has held various posts, including Deputy Director-General of the Industrial Science and Technology Policy and Environment Bureau, Senior Planning Officer for Personnel of the Secretarial Division, Minister's Secretariat; Director of the Retail and Wholesale Commerce Division, Business Support Department, Small and Medium Enterprise Agency; Director of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Division, Natural Resources and Fuel Department, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy; Director of the Automobile Division, Manufacturing Industries Bureau; Director of the Corporate Affairs Division, Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau; Director of the General Policy Division, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy; and Director of the Secretarial Division, Minister's Secretariat.In his previous role as Director-General for Natural Resources and Energy Policy, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy, he formulated export policy for energy-related infrastructure and international negotiations concerning energy policies, and established a domestic system for ensuring stable supplies of resources and energy.Mr. Hosaka previously served as Director-General of the Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau. As head of the Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau. He supervises policy planning and implementation in the areas of trade promotion, technical cooperation, investment facilitation, trade control and trade remedies.Mr. Shin Hosaka has served as Commissioner of the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2020. As head of the agency, he oversees all areas of energy policy including developing Japan’s Strategic Energy Plan, assuring secure energy supply, regulating the electricity & gas sectors, as well as promoting renewable energy and conservation.
educationInfo: Mr. Hosaka is a graduate of the University of Tokyo’s Department of Economics, Faculty of Economics, and also studied at the University of Michigan in the United States.
summary: Hosaka Shin is the Commissioner, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General for Energy and Regional Policy
careerInfo: Mr. Ozawa is a graduate of Kyoto University’s Department of Nuclear Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Graduate School of Engineering.Most recently, he helped formulate the 5th Strategic Energy Plan as the Director General for Resources and Energy Policy Coordination of the Agency for Natural Resources and Energy.While serving as Director of the Nuclear Facilities Development and Nuclear Fuel Cycle Industry Division, he worked to promote communities in areas with nuclear power stations, advance the nuclear fuel cycle policy, and develop the Nuclear Damage Compensation and Decommissioning Facilitation Corporation under the new Strategic Energy Plan following the Great East Japan Earthquake.Since joining METI, he has helped develop energy and environmental policies. While serving as Director of the Kyoto Mechanisms Office, he joined international negotiations on global warming issues in COP15 through COP17. As the Director for Energy, he formulated the first Strategic Energy Plan after the Great East Japan Earthquake.He is working to steadily promote energy and regional policies, for example by coordinating with local governments on energy policies and building cooperative relations.Mr. Ozawa Noriaki has served as Director-General for Energy and Regional Policy since July 2020.
educationInfo: Mr. Ozawa is a graduate of Kyoto University’s Department of Nuclear Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Graduate School of Engineering.
summary: Ozawa Noriaki is the Director-General for Energy and Regional Policy

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General for Policy Planning and Coordination
careerInfo: He graduated from the University of Tokyo Faculty of Law. He completed an LLM at the University of Texas.2007-2010, Director of Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI), New York: During the Lehman crisis, he oversaw the introduction of operating fund loan insurance into Japanese companies. He oversaw oil and mineral resource projects in Latin America.2010-2012, Director of the International Affairs Division, Agency for Natural Resources and Energy: He played an active role as a member of the Governing Board of the International Energy Agency (IEA). He led the emergency release of oil reserves in 2011. He concluded Japan-France and Japan-UK energy cooperation agreements.2012-2015, Director of the Oil and Gas Division: Actions he promoted include acquiring upstream interests in the UAE, successfully starting LNG exports from the United States, strengthening LNG financing, and eliminating destination-clauses in LNG trading contracts.2015-2018, Director of the Europe Division: Activities he was involved in include negotiations towards the conclusion of a Japan-EU EPA, promoting economic cooperation between Japan and Russia, and cooperating with the European Commission on regulatory matters.2018-2021, Director-General of Natural Resources and Fuel Department: His achievements include support for an LNG project in Russia (one of the largest of its kind in the world), support for structural adjustments to the oil industry, cooperation with the United States on CCUS/carbon recycling, and other decarbonization technologies, and introducing fuel ammonia.Since joining METI in 1990, his main fields of activity have been energy, the environment, and energy finance.Mr. Minami Ryo has served as Deputy Commissioner for international affairs, and Director-General for International Policy on Carbon Neutrality at the Agency of Natural Resources and Energy, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) since July 2020.  He leads the International Energy Policy as well as International Policy on Carbon Neutrality.
educationInfo: He graduated from the University of Tokyo Faculty of Law. He completed an LLM at the University of Texas.
summary: Minami Ryo is the Director-General for Policy Planning and Coordination

summary: Hamano Koichi is the Commissioner, Japan Patent Office

careerInfoDesignation: Commissioner, Small and Medium Enterprise Agency
careerInfo: Mr. Kadono graduated from the Faculty of Economics of The University of Tokyo, and from Emory University's Business School.More recently, as the Director-General of the Reconstruction Agency, he successfully established a new grant system for immigration to Fukushima.Specifically, he formed a public-private joint taskforce in 2015 to support SMEs impacted by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident. For the next three years, he led approximately 200 staff on site in Fukushima. The team visited more than 5,000 disaster-stricken businesses and provided support to help more than 1,000 SMEs resume business. Through these activities, Mr. Kadono contributed to industrial reconstruction in the disaster-stricken areas of Fukushima and to restoring trust between the affected areas and the nation.While he was Director of the Industrial Structure Policy Division Mr. Kadono formulated the vision of new industrial structure,  and during his time as Director of Kanto Bureau of Economy, Trade and Industry, he worked on support for small and medium-sized enterprises in cooperation with local governments.Mr. Kadono has held a wide range of senior posts since joining METI. They include Director of the Industrial Structure Policy Division in the Economic and Industrial Policy Bureau, Counsellor for the Manufacturing Industries Bureau, Director-General of the Kanto Bureau of Economy, Trade and Industry, and Director-General of the Reconstruction Agency.His remit includes the reconstruction of SMEs in areas affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake, promoting innovation and support for new ventures, and measures to support small businesses.Mr. Kadono Nario has served as Commissioner of the Small and Medium Enterprise Agency (SMEA) since July 2021. As the head of SMEA, he oversees all policy measures relating to SMEs in Japan.
educationInfo: Mr. Kadono graduated from the Faculty of Economics of The University of Tokyo, and from Emory University's Business School.

careerInfoDesignation: Director-General, Kanto Bureau of Economy Trade and Industry
careerInfo: More recently, while serving as Technology Policy Coordination and Industrial and Product Safety, he supervised the planning and development of government policy for technology and security, and oversaw all affairs related to them under METI’s jurisdiction.While serving as Director-General of the Research and Statistics Department, Minister’s Secretariat, METI, concurrently serving as Deputy Director-General for Policy Coordination (responsible for innovation), Minister’s Secretariat, Mr. OTA was responsible for government statistics reform, and research into technical trends that influence industrial competitiveness.During his time as Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Manufacturing Industries Bureau, METI, Mr. OTA was actively engaged in policymaking to promote the digitalization of Japan’s manufacturing industry and other efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness in this key industrial sector.While serving as Corporate Officer and Deputy Chief of the Nuclear Power and Plant Siting Division, TEPCO, Mr. OTA provided a variety of support to guide the company’s efforts, including responses to the issues at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station and the reform of the nuclear energy sector.Outside of the nuclear energy policy area, Mr. OTA served as Director of the Policy Planning and Coordination Division, Manufacturing Industries Bureau, METI; and Director-General of the Research and Statistics Department, Minister’s Secretariat, METI, while concurrently serving as Deputy Director-General for Policy Coordination, Minister’s Secretariat, Technology Policy Coordination and Industrial and Product Safety.Since joining METI, Mr. OTA has served in a wide range on senior posts. These include Deputy Director-General of the Liaison and Coordination Office, Nuclear Damage Compensation and Decommissioning Facilitation Corporation; Corporate Officer and Deputy Chief of the Nuclear Power and Plant Siting Division, Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings, Inc. (TEPCO).Mr. OTA Takehiko has served as Director-General for the Kanto Bureau of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI-Kanto) since July 2022. As the head of METI-Kanto, he leads implementation of various industrial and business policy measures. Principally, he works to match public needs with practical and effective policy measures.
educationInfo: OTA is a graduate of the University of Tokyo’s Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics
summary: Ota Takehiko is the Director-General, Kanto Bureau of Economy Trade and Industry
